function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are enforced; no “reasonable speed” exception.
• Rural highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• Urban roads: 25–45 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph during school hours. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must use a child safety seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held devices are prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules apply at intersections without signals. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• No passing on the right unless the left lane is occupied. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• No parking on sidewalks. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Registration must be displayed on the rear license plate.
• Proof of insurance must be carried. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is a “non‑moving” vehicle. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Electronic Toll Collection** | • E‑Tag (TxTag) is required for toll roads; otherwise, a toll is collected via license plate. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) – the statutory source for all traffic laws. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – provides driver’s handbook, forms, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement and guidance. **Common Enforcement Practices** - **Speeding**: Fines range from $100 to $500 plus points on the driver’s record. - **Seat‑belt Violations**: $50 fine per occupant. - **Cell‑phone Violations**: $100 fine. - **DUI**: Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. **Recent Changes (2023–2024)** - **“No‑handheld” law** extended to all vehicles, including motorcycles. - **School‑zone speed limits** increased to 25 mph in some districts. - **Electronic Toll Collection**: New “TxTag” system rolled out statewide. **Resources** - TxDMV website: https://www.txdmv.gov/ - Texas Transportation Code online: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ - Texas Highway Patrol: https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/ Feel free to let me know if you need more specific details, such as penalties for a particular offense or how to file a traffic ticket appeal.
